wedge: TOPIS planned rallies/events + road-control/incident feeds + user-chosen commute corridor or district => a mechanically derived next-morning '내 출근길 영향 있음/없음' digest with affected time window and official source links, rather than another live traffic map
last_material_result: One bounded data+action discovery round selected a new survivor after rejecting bulky-waste fee lookup as already commoditized by multiple dedicated calculators. Seoul TOPIS is a strong free/public substrate: it explicitly publishes accident/control information, weekly planned rallies/events, real-time traffic and Open APIs; Seoul's public-data pages show the traffic datasets are current and commercially reusable under attribution terms. The raw-data substitute is strong because TOPIS itself already shows live controls and planned events, so the only defensible wedge is transforming citywide feeds into a personalized tomorrow/morning commute impact answer. This action layer is mechanically derivable from location/time overlap rather than interpretive causal analysis, matching the post-kill discovery criterion. Main unresolved risk is distribution and alert delivery: maps/navigation already solve real-time routing well, and a useful proactive digest may require a lightweight scheduled backend or notification channel rather than a pure static page.
economics: KRW0 research spend. Public TOPIS/Open Data inputs appear free and commercially reusable with attribution; initial API quotas are compatible with a small prototype. Monetization would likely be indirect (ads/local mobility affiliate/cross-promotion), so expected contribution is only attractive if proactive commute-intent traffic or repeat use can be acquired cheaply. Build/maintenance is potentially low but not yet proven because scheduled alert delivery may introduce recurring infrastructure or platform dependency.
next_checkpoint: Next run: validate the proactive distribution gap, not data availability. Check whether Korean users already have a strong free 'tomorrow commute disruption' alert from Naver/Kakao/TMAP/TOPIS and whether search/community evidence exists for checking planned rallies, road controls or bus detours before commuting. Test at least 3 wedges before competition-KILL: district digest, saved-corridor impact, and event/assembly next-morning alert. KILL if incumbent navigation apps already provide equivalent proactive route-specific alerts or if the product only becomes useful with account/push infrastructure that destroys the low-maintenance economics.
recommendation: KEEP at ASSESS for one distribution/substitute round. Do not build yet. The public-data-to-action transformation is mechanically sound, but proactive acquisition/alert delivery is the make-or-break risk and must be checked before Founder Gate.
